conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Maya, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived. We’ll use a short, well-trusted questionnaire called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS for short. It’s simply 10 questions about the past seven days; your answers are completely confidential and help us make sure you’re getting the support you deserve. There are no right or wrong answers—just whatever feels true for you. Ready to start?

Over the past week, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly, not much at all. I’ve laughed maybe once or twice, and even then it felt kind of forced—like I was doing it because I knew I should, not because it felt natural. Things that used to crack me up just feel kind of flat now.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
I haven’t really. I mean, maybe once or twice I sort of chuckled, but it didn’t feel like real laughter—more like I was going through the motions. Nothing seems that funny anymore.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I try to, but most of the time I don’t really feel it. I’ll tell myself, “It’ll be nice to get out for a walk” or “It’ll be fun to Face-time my best friend,” but when the moment comes it’s kind of… meh. I still go, and once in a while I’ll get a tiny spark, but it’s nowhere near the excitement I used to have.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… pretty often. If the baby’s fussy or won’t settle, my brain jumps straight to “I must be doing something wrong.” I’ll replay every little choice—did I eat something that bothers him through the milk, did I hold him the wrong way, should I have rocked him longer? Even when my partner says it’s normal baby stuff, I still feel like it’s my fault.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Most days, yeah. I’ll be sitting there feeding him and suddenly my heart’s racing because I’m sure he’s too quiet—so I’m poking him to check he’s breathing. Or I’ll lie awake imagining the stroller tipping, or him choking, even though none of that’s happening. I know in my head it’s unlikely, but I can’t switch the worry off.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes I get that sudden wave—like my chest tightens and I feel shaky for no real reason. It happened twice this week: once while I was folding laundry and once in the grocery line. No warning, just this rush of “something awful is about to happen,” and I have to stand there breathing hard until it passes.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… a lot of the time. I’ll look at the sink full of bottles, the laundry pile, the texts I haven’t answered, and feel like I’m drowning. I still push through because the baby needs me, but it’s like I’m barely treading water most days.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes. I lie down exhausted, but my head keeps circling—worrying I forgot something, replaying every cry, picturing worst-case scenarios. It takes me over an hour to fall asleep most nights, and then I wake up two or three times with my heart pounding, sure I heard the baby even when he’s quiet. By morning I feel like I never really rested.
I have felt sad or miserable

Pretty much every day this week. I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling that just sits on me. I’ll look at the baby and feel like I should be glowing, but instead I feel empty or on the verge of tears. It lifts a little if someone visits or if the sun’s out, but it always settles back in.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… it’s happened twice this week. Yesterday I just looked at the pile of unfolded laundry and started sobbing, and the day before I cried in the shower because I felt like I was failing at everything. The tears kind of come out of nowhere and once they start it’s hard to stop.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

I… I have had that thought pop in a couple of times—like, “What if I just weren’t here?”—but I never plan anything, and I don’t want to leave my baby. It’s more this fleeting, scary picture that shows up when everything feels too heavy, and then I shove it away and feel guilty for even thinking it.

You've shared how the joy of new motherhood feels clouded by a heavy gray mood, constant worry, and a sense that you're barely treading water. <quote>I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling</quote> captures the exhaustion and sadness that have become daily companions, while fleeting thoughts of <quote>What if I just weren't here?</quote> highlight just how overwhelmed you feel right now.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 26, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>Patient describes inability to experience genuine laughter and loss of humor, aligning with "Not at all"</sym>, <sym>Patient reports markedly reduced anticipatory enjoyment—she still attempts activities but feels "meh" and only rarely a "tiny spark," clearly aligning with "Definitely less than I used to."</sym>, <sym>Patient reports frequent self-blame, replaying choices and feeling at fault despite reassurance, matching "Yes, most of the time"</sym>, <sym>Patient worries daily and cannot stop intrusive thoughts, matching 'Yes, very often</sym>, <sym>Describes sudden, unexpected panic episodes occurring twice this week with physical symptoms and dread, aligning with "Yes, sometimes"</sym>, <sym>She describes feeling overwhelmed "a lot of the time," unable to manage daily tasks, and "barely treading water," matching the highest level of not coping.</sym>, <sym>Patient describes nightly sleep disruption with racing thoughts, multiple awakenings, and lack of rest, aligning with 'most of the time'.</sym>, <sym>Patient describes daily, persistent sadness with heaviness and emptiness despite occasional brief relief, aligning with "Yes, most of the time"</sym>, <sym>Patient describes two crying episodes triggered by minor stressors, indicating frequent but not constant tearfulness</sym>, <sym>Patient describes intrusive, passive suicidal thoughts ('What if I just weren't here?') that occur occasionally ('a couple of times') but denies intent or planning, aligning with the 'Sometimes' option.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** A score of 26 on the EPDS places you well above the clinical cutoff; any score ≥14 or a positive response on Item 10 warrants urgent evaluation. You described <sym>depressed mood</sym> most days, marked <sym>loss of interest</sym>, <sym>sleep disruption</sym>, <sym>guilt</sym>, and <sym>recurrent thoughts of death</sym>, meeting <med>DSM-5</med> criteria for <med>Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange same-day appointment with your <med>obstetrician</med>, <med>primary care provider</med>, or local <med>perinatal mental health team</med>
2. Ask about evidence-based treatments such as <med>CBT</med>, <med>IPT</med>, or <med>sertraline</med> compatible with breastfeeding
3. Create a safety plan: list 24/7 supports like the <med>National Maternal Mental Health Hotline</med> (1-833-943-5746) and local crisis line
4. Enlist practical help-trusted adult to handle night bottles, meals, or laundry so you can rest
5. Practice 5-minute grounding exercises when panic surges; try paced breathing (4-7-8 count)
6. Schedule a follow-up EPDS in two weeks to track progress after starting support
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 26: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary  
Patient: Postpartum mother (infant  ≤ 6 mo)

Date:

Source: Self-report questionnaire

Symptoms endorsed:
- Marked anhedonia, loss of pleasure in daily & social activities  
- Depressed mood most days, frequent crying spells  
- Sleep disturbance (initial & middle insomnia) directly related to persistent worry & low mood  
- Excessive self-blame / guilt concerning infant care  
- Generalized anxiety with episodic panic-like surges (no clear trigger)  
- Feeling overwhelmed, “drowning” in routine tasks  
- Passive suicidal ideation (“What if I weren’t here?”) without plan or intent

Pattern: Symptoms present “most days,” duration ≥ past 2 weeks.  
Functional impact: Difficulty completing household tasks, impaired rest, emotional dysregulation.

Screening flags:
A. Probable major depressive episode, peripartum onset  
B. Comorbid anxiety symptoms meeting clinical threshold  
C. Safety: Self-harm ideas reported → warrants immediate risk assessment

Recommendation: Refer for comprehensive psychiatric evaluation; consider EPDS completion and same-day safety planning.

Clinician signature / credentials
